visual: Large evergreen shrub or small tree with dense glossy dark green, leathery, strongly aromatic leaves; small pale greenish-yellow flowers appear in spring and female plants may later carry glossy black berries.
water: Water regularly while establishing and keep container plants evenly watered; established plants tolerate moderate dry periods.
aspect: North, east, south or west-facing; full sun to partial shade.
soil: Well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral and alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and exposed frost pockets, particularly for plants grown in containers.
prune: Requires little pruning if grown naturally; trim in spring or summer to maintain hedges, topiary or a compact shape.
toxicity: Leaves are widely used as a culinary herb; fruits are ornamental and should not be eaten. Gloves are advisable when handling.
resilience: Hardy through most of the UK when established, particularly in the ground; container-grown specimens are more vulnerable to severe frost.
uses: Culinary herb, evergreen screening, hedging, topiary, containers, courtyard gardens, coastal planting and Mediterranean-style schemes.
